inline.label: Six contraceptive devices drawn to one common scale of 23 pixels per centimeter: a diaphragm 7 centimeters across, a cervical cap 3 centimeters, a contraceptive sponge 5.5 centimeters with a removal loop, a T-shaped intrauterine device 3.2 centimeters tall with two strings, an implant rod 4 centimeters long and 2 millimeters thick, and a vaginal ring 5.4 centimeters across. Each is labeled with how long it may stay in place.
inline.abbr: What each one looks like — all six at one scale = 1 cm, on every drawing below Diaphragm · 7 cm shallow dome with a springy rim in 6 h before → out by 24 h Cervical cap · 3 cm deeper, and less than half as wide max 48 h Sponge · 5.5 cm dimple one side, loop the other 30 h total — an absolute ceiling Vaginal ring · 5.4 cm soft, and not felt once it is in 3 weeks in, 1 week out IUD · 3.2 cm tall a T, with two strings through the cervix stays for years shown at its real size Implant · 4 cm × 2 mm one rod, under the skin of the upper arm stays for years

inline.label: Diagram of the HIV virion: gp120 and gp41 spikes on the envelope, two strands of RNA and three enzymes inside the capsid
inline.abbr: One virus, four things to know capsid gp120 tip grabs CD4 gp41 stem does fusion 2 strands of RNA  — not DNA 3 enzymes:  RT, integrase, protease

inline.title: Attachment
inline.label: HIV drifts up to a CD4 T cell and its gp120 knob grabs the CD4 receptor
inline.abbr: CD4 T cell HIV gp120 CD4 CCR5

inline.title: Fusion
inline.label: gp41 acts as a grappling hook, pulling the two membranes together so the capsid can slide in

inline.title: Reverse transcription
inline.label: Reverse transcriptase copies the virus RNA into DNA and makes typos as it goes
inline.abbr: RT ! typos here RNA reverse transcriptase DNA

inline.title: Integration
inline.label: Integrase staples the HIV DNA into the cell chromosome, where it stays for life
inline.abbr: integrase HIV DNA your DNA your DNA

inline.title: Protein production
inline.label: The cell reads the HIV DNA and builds virus parts as one long protein chain
inline.abbr: nucleus mRNA ribosome one long protein

inline.title: Budding
inline.label: A new virus particle pushes out through the cell membrane and floats away wrapped in the cell own coat
inline.abbr: not infectious yet your cell membrane

inline.title: Maturation
inline.label: Protease cuts the long protein into working parts and the particle becomes infectious

inline.title: Burn depth and skin layers
inline.label: A cross-section through skin showing epidermis, dermis and subcutaneous fat with a hair follicle, sebaceous gland, sweat gland, capillary loop and nerve endings. Four vertical zones show how deep each burn depth reaches: superficial burns damage only the epidermis and are painful and red; superficial partial thickness burns reach the upper dermis and blister and are very painful; deep partial thickness burns reach the lower dermis, look waxy and mottled and are less painful; full thickness burns destroy all skin layers into the fat, look dry and leathery and are painless because the nerve endings are gone.
inline.abbr: How deep each burn goes — and why the deep ones stop hurting red · dry · no blister wet, weeping blisters waxy, blotchy red and white dry, leathery eschar surface epidermis papillary dermis reticular dermis subcutaneous fat muscle hair sebaceous sweat gland capillary nerve endings deep nerve destroyed destroyed destroyed destroyed Superficial first degree epidermis only PAINFUL heals ~1 week, no scar Superficial partial second degree into the upper dermis VERY PAINFUL blisters · heals 2–3 weeks Deep partial second degree into the lower dermis LESS painful scars · may need grafting Full thickness third degree all layers, into the fat PAINLESS always needs grafting Painless is the frightening one. A burn that does not hurt has burned through the nerve endings — that is depth, not comfort. And superficial burns are  never counted  in the rule of nines or in Parkland — you start at partial thickness.
